newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar trades narrower range, ends near highs.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar trades narrower range, ends near highs.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed near its highs in a very quiet market, pausing for breath after days of nervous, whippy trade and political drama.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6972/79 and 66.42 on its Trade-Weighted Index from 0.6961/68 and 66.39 in early trade.
The currency ground higher over the day and dealers said there were some options plays, with reasonable interest on both sides.
One dealer said the bias was probably to drift somewhat higher in a market that was still short, but another said people were looking to sell into any rallies.

The currency appeared to have settled into a 0.6950-85 range, about a cent lower than before populist Winston Peters exercised the balance of power by taking his New Zealand First Party into a centre-right coalition with the conservative National Party.

Markets are relatively comfortable with a planned NZ$5 billion of extra spending over three years, given the deferral of next year's tax cuts by a year and the fact the coalition will still be running budget surpluses. But there is still some unease over the power that Peters will wield as Treasurer.
The market was gearing up for next Tuesday's Monetary Policy Statement by the Reserve Bank but with little expectation of any further easing.
"It does seem a rather large easing already is in place, both in the currency and the rates," one dealer said.
